project_overview: This project appears to be a web application likely related to education or student management, judging by the file names and component structures. It utilizes Vue.js for the front-end and contains components related to student information, exam submissions, and potentially admissions. The codebase demonstrates a layered architecture with distinct components, suggesting a focus on modularity and maintainability. The audit aims to assess the overall health of this application, highlighting potential vulnerabilities and areas for improvement.

macro_trends.title: High-Level View Import Vulnerability
macro_trends.description: Several Vue components directly import higher-level components (e.g., `iLikeCoursesNew.vue` importing `ApplicationServices.vue`), potentially leading to brittle dependencies and difficulties in managing component hierarchy. This introduces a significant risk if component structures change, causing cascading issues.

macro_trends.title: State Management Fragility
macro_trends.description: Deep prop-drilling suggests potential state management issues. Without a centralized state management solution (e.g., Vuex), maintaining consistent data across components could become complex and error-prone, particularly as the application grows. This is further highlighted by the layering concerns.

key_workflows.name: Student Data Flow
key_workflows.description: This workflow involves retrieving student data from the data access layer, processing it within the business logic layer, and rendering it in the presentation layer (Vue components). The audit focuses on identifying potential vulnerabilities within this critical data path, especially concerning prop-drilling and potential inconsistencies.
